notes: Counts are recorded exactly as each source states them for a specific year's paper; nothing is estimated or summed by us. 'outOf' is what the source says for that table: 50 per subject for 2021-2024 analyses that count all 50 questions (Section A 35 + Section B 15 incl. the 5 optional ones), 45 where the source counts 45 attempted questions (physics/chemistry 2019, 2020, 2025, 2026 re-exam), 90 for combined biology tables, null where the source does not state a total (all multi-year tables). Every table has a 'tables' entry with its own row sum so you can see when a source's rows do not add to the stated total. Entries with componentOfMerged=true are several source rows that map to the same chapter of ours within one source/year/paper (e.g. PW 'Rotational Motion' + 'Center of Mass and System of Particles' -> our System of Particles and Rotational Motion; 'Circular Motion' -> Motion in a Plane): the consumer must SUM them. Chapter names are mapped to our 79 ids; source rows that span several of our chapters (Optics, Electrostatics, Kinematics, p-block ...), chapters not in our list (p-block, s-block, metallurgy, solid state, Transport in Plants, Digestion ...) and unit-level rows go to 'unmapped' with a reason. Zero counts for mapped chapters are kept (a listed 0 is a statement); unmapped zero rows are dropped. Sources count section placement differently (e.g. PW puts Biomolecules, Biotechnology and Evolution under Zoology/Botany differently from our ids); entries are assigned by chapter id, with the source's own placement in subjectSection. 2026 has two papers: 'cancelled-3-may' (cancelled after a leak) and 're-exam-21-june'; Careers360's 2026 column is unlabelled and kept as '2026-unspecified'. Multi-year tables (Collegedunia, PW weightage pages, Careers360, Testbook) disagree with PW's own per-paper analyses for several years; all are kept. Several sources are copies of each other (Vedantu/Byjus/Unacademy 2021; Testbook 2023-2025 = PW weightage table). Excluded: multi-year averages / 'expected' tables (Allen, Aakash, Motion, iQuanta, PW 'Average Count' columns, Embibe 2020 percentages) and PW 2023 chemistry (identical to an Allen average table).
